topic: the mass ceiling that stops black holes from growing forever (TON 618)
title: Physics Says Black Holes Can't Grow Past 50 Billion Suns
description: Astrophysicist Andrew King worked out the largest mass a black hole can actually reach before its own fuel source falls apart. TON 618 is one of the few known objects sitting close enough to that number to test the idea for real.

hook_candidates.text: Most people think black holes eat forever -- physics actually caps them at 50 billion Suns.
What actually stops a black hole from growing forever? Its own food supply collapses on itself first.
Black holes don't just keep growing as long as there's matter nearby -- past a certain mass, they run out of fuel by design.
In 2015, one astrophysicist calculated the exact weight a black hole could never grow past -- and we'd already found one sitting right at it.

payoff_mechanism: A black hole grows by feeding on a spinning disc of gas, but once the black hole passes roughly fifty billion solar masses that disc becomes too massive to hold together and collapses into stars, cutting off the fuel it needs to keep growing.
share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who insists black holes just swallow everything forever, because they want to finally prove them wrong.
contradicted_belief: Most people think a black hole can keep eating and growing forever without ever hitting a limit.

sources.note: University of Leicester (Andrew King): black holes cap out near 50 billion solar masses before their feeding disc collapses into stars.
Andrew King, 'How Big Can a Black Hole Grow?' -- derives the ~5x10^10 solar-mass accretion limit.

beats.text: Most people think black holes eat forever -- physics actually caps them at **50 billion** Suns.
Get one too massive and its own gas disc **collapses** into stars instead of fuel.
TON 618 already sits at that same **50-billion-Sun** wall -- follow for the next one.
